subject: Planned: West US rolling network/firmware cascade - Apr 5 (low-risk, brief reconnects)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@acme-analytics.com>, ops@acme-analytics.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-30T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Planned: West US rolling network/firmware cascade - Apr 5 (low-risk, brief reconnects)

Hi Nora / Acme ops team,

We wanted to give you an early heads-up about a planned rolling firmware update for West US inference nodes on Monday, Apr 5. This is a targeted network/NIC firmware and driver refresh that is part of our ongoing stability program.

Window
- Start: 2027-04-05 04:00 UTC
- End: 2027-04-05 08:00 UTC
- Expected per-instance disruption: 20-90 seconds while the NIC firmware reloads and the host performs health checks. Instances are restarted in a staggered fashion so your overall capacity should remain available.

Scope
- Region: West US (us-west1)
- Affects: Inference pods running on dedicated and hosted pools in the region
- Impact: brief TCP connection resets; well-benchmarked for no request loss when clients retry idempotently. Latency spikes for in-flight streams are possible during the ~1m window per node.

Mitigation and runbook highlights
- We will perform a rolling update with max concurrency of 2% of capacity per wave.
- Health checks will keep traffic off nodes until they pass warmup probes.
- KV/prefix caches are preserved where possible; model KV caches will be warmed on restart.
- For critical flows, route preference can be shifted to a secondary region (we can coordinate if you want us to failover during the window).

Attachments: firmware-notes-v3.pdf (release notes), scheduled-runbook.txt (operator checklist)

If you have a hard restriction on that window, please let us know by EOD Friday (Apr 2) and we will work with you to adjust. Otherwise we'll proceed with the plan.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Site Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: firmware-notes-v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Nora Patel <nora@acme-analytics.com>

Date: 2027-03-31T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned: West US rolling network/firmware cascade - Apr 5 (low-risk, brief reconnects)

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the heads-up. A couple of quick questions from our side:
1) Can you confirm the maximum concurrent restart rate (you mentioned 2% but wanted the explicit number of hosts per wave for our fleet size ~600 nodes)?
2) We run low-latency streaming for scoring (non-idempotent). Are there safeguards for in-flight streams (will the proxy keep connections or will we see resets)?

If there's any chance of moving the window earlier on Apr 5 (UTC 02:00-06:00) that would be preferable for our downstream batch pipelines; otherwise we'll plan for retries on our side.

Best,
Nora
Nora Patel
Head of Platform
Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Planned: West US rolling network/firmware cascade - Apr 5 (low-risk, brief reconnects)

Hi Nora — good questions, thanks.

Answers:
- Concurrency: 2% of active inference hosts per wave ~= 12 hosts per wave (for your referenced 600-node equivalent). We run waves every 6 minutes and will pause immediately if error rates increase.
- In-flight streams: the proxy will attempt graceful drain; however, we do expect some TCP resets for mid-flight streams. Our recommendation for non-idempotent streaming is to enable our stream-resume fallback (we can toggle a short buffering window at the edge for your routes during the window). If you'd like us to enable it, confirm and we'll schedule the toggle for the maintenance window.

We can start the window earlier (02:00 UTC) as you requested. Proposed revised window: 2027-04-05 02:00 - 06:00 UTC. Please confirm and we will update the runbook.

- Marcus

Date: 2027-04-06T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Completed: West US maintenance - brief summary and telemetry

Hi Nora / Acme ops,

Thanks again for coordinating. Maintenance completed on 2027-04-05 with the revised 02:00-06:00 UTC window. Summary below and attachments with telemetry and a short draft postmortem attached.

What we ran
- Rolling NIC firmware and driver refresh across westus dedicated and hosted pools
- Concurrency: 12 hosts/wave (2%); waves every 6 minutes
- Edge stream-resume fallback enabled for your routes during the window per your request

Observed impact
- Majority of waves completed without issue.
- We observed transient TCP resets on ~3% of hosts during the driver handshake; total affected pods ~18 (~3% of the subset we measured). Most of these recovered within 45-80s.
- No customer-visible request-level errors were recorded for Acme's tracked routes; retry logic and the edge stream-resume prevented request loss for your critical flows.
- A small number of in-flight streams required client reconnects; we flagged those and included trace ids in the attached telemetry.

Follow-ups / next steps
- We've attached maintenance-telemetry.csv (per-wave success/failure counts) and a postmortem draft (postmortem-draft.md).
- Ops will review telemetry and propose a mitigation to reduce driver-handshake resets in the next firmware candidate (action: Monica).
- If you want a dedicated call to walk through traces and any customer-side reconnects, we're available; suggest Thu Apr 8 16:00 UTC.

Attachments: maintenance-telemetry.csv, postmortem-draft.md

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Site Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
